ember.promise: A little ember ruff promises a crown of fire.
ember.payoff: The adolescent holds the heat in uneven seams; the final crown opens around the same wolf.
ember.corrections: Approved final silhouette direction. Reconcile round base ears, spot-to-chevron landmarks and rendering style. The image formerly called Pyremane is used as the proposed Blazefang payoff direction under EVO-0, not a renamed game asset.

stages.name: Cindercub
stages.label: Base / banked embers
stages.note: Grounded pup; keep the ruff restrained.

stages.name: Smoulderpup
stages.label: Middle / working name
stages.note: Lanky and scruffy; ember seams, but no open fire crown.

stages.name: Blazefang
stages.label: Final / approved visual direction
stages.note: The shoulder ruff opens into the spectacular crown.

tide.promise: A little folded frill promises command of the river.
tide.payoff: The gangly middle carries floppy fin folds; the final unfurls them into a great wave crown on a flowing river-reptile body.
tide.corrections: Candidate final. Retain cheek sacs, face and ring landmarks through all stages; shorten any excessive neck stretch and verify four legs. Water arc is elemental reference detail, not a collision footprint.

stages.name: Ripplet
stages.label: Base / practising water
stages.note: Curious small river lizard; neck-fold promise still needs a restrained redraw.

stages.name: Riverwisp
stages.label: Middle / working name
stages.note: Long-legged, half-grown frill drooping beside the neck.

stages.name: Tidewyrm
stages.label: Final / payoff candidate
stages.note: Folded fins become a wave crest; same river-reptile identity.

grove.promise: A little moss bed promises a whole living grove.
grove.payoff: The middle garden grows uneven saplings; the final carries a broad tree canopy with the familiar nest still sheltered among its roots.
grove.corrections: Candidate final. Thorn crown must grow from the shoulder vegetation, not read as deer antlers; fix speckle/ear landmarks and make the canopy’s attachment and weight believable. Do not hide the boar under vegetation.

stages.name: Mosshog
stages.label: Base / first moss garden
stages.note: Small boar with a moss bed and nesting space.

stages.name: Thicketboar
stages.label: Middle / working name
stages.note: Burly and overgrown, with uneven thin saplings rather than a full canopy.

stages.name: Thornback
stages.label: Final / payoff candidate
stages.note: A walking grove; animal remains the solid foundation.
